clue.text: Plunder or spoil gold and diamonds

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
D is the card-game abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A list of crimes: robbing a place or ruining its jewellery store of gold and diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To maraud is to roam about raiding, a verb synonym for plundering.

clue.text: Detest August Bank Holiday on roads, for starters

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so only the first letter of each word is wanted

parts.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone who hates driving on the busy roads of the late-summer public holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The August Bank Holiday is a British public holiday, famous for traffic jams.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor is to loathe, a straightforward verb synonym for detest.

clue.text: The dummy of the family who's likely to get some stick?

definitions.text: The dummy of the family who's likely to get some stick?

parts.words: The dummy of the family who's likely to get some stick?
parts.note: surface reading: the family idiot, the relative everyone criticises
setter's reading: a fairground figure that people literally throw sticks at, named like a relative

explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a wooden figure in a traditional British pub or fair game, knocked with thrown sticks; figuratively, anyone set up for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairground target is both a dummy and, by name, a family member, and taking stick means suffering criticism.

clue.text: Radio station employee picked up formal attire

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by the ear, as a radio picks up a signal

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket, evening wear

explanation.surface: A worker at a radio station collected a tuxedo from the cleaners.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ stands for both dinner jacket and disc jockey; the answer is the second spelled out as it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: A deejay plays records on air, so is someone employed at a radio station.

clue.text: Plucky leaders of Premier League advanced new strategy

parts.note: game means brave and willing

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters

parts.note: first letters of the two words
A is a standard abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Brave club bosses in English top-flight football push forward a new tactical approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A game plan is an overall plan of action, so a strategy.

clue.text: Jason quite possibly man's best friend?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Greek hero who brought back the Golden Fleece
second meaning: a breed of dog

explanation.walkthrough: Jason recovered the Golden Fleece, so he could be called a fetcher of something golden; the same phrase names a popular dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog is the proverbial best friend of man, and the breed name read literally describes Jason's quest.

clue.text: Gruelling event mum organised involving hot pants

indicators.note: pants is slang for rubbish, so the word before it is in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one part is placed inside another

parts.note: ran as in ran an event, managed it
the word hot, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiring race whose mother-organiser includes hot pants in the kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish; here it shuffles the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a 26-mile race, the archetypal exhausting contest.

clue.text: Rice dish feeds Dua Lipa when travelling north

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling north means reading from bottom to top
the dish feeds the singer by sitting inside her name, tucked within the letters

parts.note: letters inside the singer's name

explanation.surface: The pop star Dua Lipa eats a rice dish while on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau is rice cooked in stock with spices, a dish from South Asia and the Middle East.

clue.text: Indifferent article sadly inadequate

parts.note: the indefinite article
pathetic means miserably inadequate

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that is neither good nor bad, just woefully weak.
explanation.walkthrough: Indifferent looks like a judgement of the article's quality, but it is the definition: lacking interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Apathetic means showing no interest or concern, a synonym of indifferent.

clue.text: Caught Rachel on broadcast defending pound? It's her job!

definitions.note: her refers to Rachel, the UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves

indicators.note: defending means guarding by surrounding, so one part goes around another
broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: c is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
taken as written for the shuffle
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Rachel, on the radio defending sterling: that is what the Chancellor does.
explanation.walkthrough: Rachel Reeves became Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer in 2024, the finance minister whose job includes defending the pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue's Rachel is Rachel Reeves, whose cabinet post is finance minister, so the title is her job.

clue.text: Live heavy metal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as in to ... a quiet life
second meaning: the dense grey element

explanation.walkthrough: Heavy metal suggests loud rock music played live; here the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead a life is to live it, and the chemical element Pb is a classic heavy metal.

clue.text: City police nab Sir Bernard after going over cases

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the letters run backwards
a case is an outer covering, so the words here enclose the target

parts.note: the run of letters from the end of police to the start of Bernard

explanation.surface: Officers arrest a knight called Bernard after he went through their files.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards across the end of police, nab, Sir and the first letter of Bernard.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the capital city of the Australian state of Queensland.

clue.text: Sensitive spot at the rear that hurts Yankee

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of the word
the cry of someone in pain
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American has a tender patch on his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Spot at the rear reads like a sore bottom, but it means only the last letter of spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Touchy means easily offended or tender to the touch, matching sensitive.

clue.text: Stone wall stripped following work

indicators.note: stripped means peeled bare, so the outer letters are taken off

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: Builders working on a stone wall have stripped it back.
explanation.definitionFit: An opal is a semi-precious gemstone, and stone in crosswords often means a gem.

clue.text: One demonstrating in favour of examiner

parts.note: pro means for or in support of
a tester examines things

explanation.surface: Someone running a demonstration in support of an inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: A protester takes part in a public demonstration against something.

clue.text: Joey had dinner, hosting married male person he shares with

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so one part takes another into it

parts.note: a joey is a baby kangaroo, and roo is short for kangaroo
had a meal
m is the abbreviation for married
m is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Joey has a married man round for dinner, the man he lives with.
explanation.walkthrough: Joey suggests the character from Friends, who shares a flat; here it is a young kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A roommate is someone who shares your room or flat, so the person he shares with.

clue.text: Kerry and Emma going out to have a good time

indicators.note: going out suggests a night of wild behaviour, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: the two names, letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Two friends are heading out on the town for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry is an idiom for celebrating and enjoying oneself.

clue.text: Father nearly cut piece of 22 Down writing

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Father is a priest, a cleric
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A priest almost cut a section of humorous writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 Down is COMIC, so the definition is a piece of comic writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a four-line humorous verse about a famous person, a form of comic writing.

clue.text: Golly! Top performing linguist

indicators.note: performing suggests putting on an act, so these letters play a new role in a new order

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of amazement at a brilliant linguist's show.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyglot speaks many languages, so is a linguist in the everyday sense.

clue.text: Thrill that comes after firing a gun?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a buzz of excitement

definitions.text: that comes after firing a gun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the jolt of recoil

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the excitement after shooting, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: One gets a kick out of something exciting, and a gun's backward jolt on firing is also called its kick.

clue.text: 20d cut

parts.note: a score is twenty
the letter as written

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a self-reference to its own number, but 20 is a number and d a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, so scored means cut or incised.

clue.text: Where Yorkshire folk are racing Ferrari, iconically?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a seaside town in North Yorkshire
second meaning, split 3,3: Ferrari's famous racing colour on a vehicle

explanation.surface: Wondering where northerners are watching a famous Italian racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferrari race cars are traditionally painted red.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcar is a coastal town in North Yorkshire, England, where Yorkshire people live.

clue.text: Universal sacking Head of Studio? That's funny

indicators.note: sacking means firing, so the first letter of the named word is removed

parts.note: cosmic means of the universe
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A film company fires its studio boss, and someone finds it amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal is capitalised to look like the Hollywood studio; it means relating to the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means funny, so saying 'that's comic' is saying 'that's funny'.

clue.text: Secretly destabilising American

indicators.note: destabilising throws something off balance, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A covert operation to undermine someone from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal Latin phrase for proceedings held in private, so secretly.

clue.text: Resistance provided the French weapon

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
provided that, so if
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French Resistance was supplied with arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun, a type of weapon.

clue.text: Stop baseball team making a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the name runs back the way it came

parts.note: the New York Mets

explanation.surface: Halting a struggling baseball side's attempt to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem a flow is to stop or check it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Husband finished carbon boat that skims the waves

parts.note: h is the abbreviation for husband
over means ended
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
a raft is a simple flat boat

explanation.surface: A man finishes building a carbon-fibre boat that skims the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses boat, which also supplies a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovercraft rides on a cushion of air just above the water, gliding over it.

clue.text: While rapping, Snoop cursed High Street competition

indicators.note: rapping is speaking rhythmically, so the words are judged by their spoken sound

parts.note: to snoop is to pry
cursed means swore

explanation.surface: The rapper Snoop Dogg swears in his lyrics about shops competing.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoop looks like the rapper's name; it is a verb meaning pry. Said together, pry swore runs into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A price war is when rival retailers keep cutting prices, competition on the shopping street.

clue.text: Poet's humourless study

parts.note: dry means dull, lacking fun
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: A poet's study is dull and joyless.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a seventeenth-century English poet and the first Poet Laureate.
